cards.explanation: The answer is a sign. Some of the scribes, the teachers of the law, and some Pharisees say to Jesus, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.” The text doesn't tell us why they ask, friends. I'll leave that open, because the text does.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “…none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” So this generation is not getting nothing, friends. It gets one sign, and Jesus names it right there.

The answer is Jonah. Jesus says none will be given “…except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” Jonah is the prophet we meet in the book that carries his name. He's the one Jesus points to in the very next verse.

The answer is three days and three nights. Jesus says, “For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish…” Three days, three nights, no rounding up, friends. That number is the whole point of the comparison He's about to make.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.” The 'as' and the 'so' line the two up. Same length of time for both.

The answer is that they repented at the preaching of Jonah. Jesus says the men of Nineveh will condemn this generation, “for they repented at the preaching of Jonah…” They heard the message and repented, friends. Jesus sets that beside a generation that's asking for a sign.

The answer is greater. Jesus says, “…and now One greater than Jonah is here.” He's talking about Himself, friends. Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching, and One greater than Jonah is standing right in front of these people.

The answer is the wisdom of Solomon. Jesus says the Queen of the South “…came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon…” Solomon was a king of Israel, and people came from every nation to hear his wisdom (1 Kings 4:34). She made a long trip just to listen, bakers.

The answer is False. Jesus says the unclean spirit “…passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.” It goes looking and comes up empty, friends. That's what sets up the spirit's next move.

The answer is empty and swept clean. Jesus says the spirit finds the house “…vacant, swept clean, and put in order.” Nobody's home, and everything's tidy. I've seen a spotless counter in my day, friends, and it didn't mean anyone was cooking.

The answers are seven and worse. Jesus says the spirit “…brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself…” That's seven more, and each one is more wicked than the first spirit. They all go in together. Then Jesus says, “And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.” The man ends up in a harder spot than where he began, friends. Jesus then says this is how it will be with this wicked generation.

The answer is this wicked generation. After the picture of the spirit and the house, Jesus says, “So will it be with this wicked generation.” He ties the picture back to this wicked generation, friends. That's where the whole picture was heading.

The answer is True. Someone tells Jesus His mother and brothers are outside, and He answers, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?” Two questions in one breath, friends. He doesn't just say yes or no.

The answer is disciples. The text says Jesus pointed to His disciples, and then He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers.” Disciples are the people who follow Jesus, bakers. He points right at them as He says it.

The answer is whoever does the will of His Father. Jesus says, “For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.” He's talking about doing the will of His Father in heaven, friends. Whoever does that is family to Him.
